lessons.content_body: Please review the official course syllabus thoroughly. It outlines all expectations, weekly milestones, and academic integrity policies.

lessons.title: Lecture 1: Principles of Cloud Distributed Systems
lessons.description: Prof. Maryam breaks down modern distributed systems, scale-out versus scale-up models, and latency numbers every engineer should know.
lessons.content_body:
### Lecture Summary

In this session, we investigate fundamental tradeoffs in distributed computing.

Key Concepts:
- Single point of failure vs high availability
- Network partitions and fail-stop vs Byzantine failure modes
- The Eight Fallacies of Distributed Computing

lessons.title: Lecture 1 Slides: Distributed Foundations & CAP Theorem
lessons.description: Full lecture presentation slides covering CAP theorem trade-offs and consensus models.
lessons.content_body: Presentation slides from Week 1. Review slides 12 through 28 before attempting the module quiz.

lessons.title: Lecture 2: Container Internals (Namespaces & Cgroups)
lessons.description: Deep architectural dive into Linux namespaces (PID, Mount, Net), cgroups resource throttling, and union overlay filesystems.
lessons.content_body:
### Deep Dive: Container Mechanics

Containers are isolated processes, not lightweight virtual machines. In this lecture, we construct a mini-container using chroot, unshare, and cgroups v2.

lessons.title: Architecture Notes: Kubernetes Control Plane & Etcd Consensus
lessons.description: Comprehensive reference guide to kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and etcd.
lessons.content_body:
# Kubernetes Control Plane Deep Dive

The Kubernetes control plane makes global decisions about the cluster (for example, scheduling), as well as detecting and responding to cluster events.

## 1. kube-apiserver
The API server is the front end for the Kubernetes control plane. It exposes the Kubernetes API and is designed to scale horizontally.

## 2. etcd
Consistent and highly-available key value store used as Kubernetes backing store for all cluster data.

lessons.description: Mathematical proofs of maximum height O(log N) and rotation invariants in red-black trees.

lessons.description: Implementation of Dijkstra with Fibonacci heap priority queue for O(E + V log V) optimal runtime.
lessons.content_body: Visual walkthrough of shortest path relaxation.

lessons.content_body: Detailed mathematical derivations for vector-Jacobian products.

lessons.title: Lecture 2: Self-Attention & Transformer Blocks

lessons.content_body: Comprehensive overview of multi-head attention mechanisms.

assignments.title: Assignment 1: Distributed Object Storage Ring Implementation
assignments.instructions: Build a robust, distributed key-value chunk store implementing Consistent Hashing with virtual nodes (128 per physical node). Include replication factor R=3 with quorum read/write consistency (W=2, R=2). Submit your source code archive (.zip) and an executive performance report (.pdf).

assignments.title: Lab 1: Red-Black Tree Implementation & Benchmark
assignments.instructions: Implement a generic self-balancing red-black tree with insertion, deletion, and interval queries in C++ or Rust. Submit performance benchmarks against standard library std::map.

assignments.title: Lab 1: Neural Autodiff Engine in NumPy
assignments.instructions: Construct a modular micro-framework implementing Tensor nodes, forward evaluation, backward pass with backward hooks, and SGD optimizer.

quizzes.description: Comprehensive examination testing your understanding of consistency models, CAP theorem, replication topologies, and container orchestration.
